newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar ends off at 489.25/490.25/dlr.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar ends off at 489.25/490.25/dlr.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar weakened for the eighth straight session closing at 489.25/490.25 per dollar in nervous trade.

But morning losses that saw the bolivar fall as far as 490.75 per dollar were pared after the Central Bank announced a large 200 billion bolivar TEM auction for Wednesday, which prompted dollar inflows from foreign investors, traders said.
The bolivar closed Monday at 488.75/489.75 per dollar.
"The market was very nervous in the morning with a lot of corporate dollar buying after the bolivar fell through the psychological 490/dollar barrier," said one trader.
But: "after a shaky morning, the bolivar firmed again in the afternoon after the Central Bank announced the TEMs sale ... foreign investors began to move into bolivars," said another trader.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
